transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... well, I guess I just keep making these small mistakes. Like on my applications, or my research notes. It's... kind of embarrassing, honestly. I'll mislabel an artwork date or just skip a question entirely. And the thing is, I really thought I had checked them over before turning them in. So... yeah. That's what finally made me come in.
Do you notice that you have trouble staying focused or your mind wanders during many different activities—not just when reviewing your work—like during conversations, reading, or meetings?

Yeah... I guess so. Um, mostly when I'm trying to read or write at my desk. It doesn't take much. Like... a siren outside, or just someone talking in the hallway. Or even just a random thought about an exhibit idea. I'll just... drift off. And then twenty minutes will go by before I even notice I stopped working. So, yeah.
Thinking back to when you were a kid, in grade school for example, did you notice similar problems with staying focused, careless mistakes, or getting easily distracted?

Um... yeah, I guess so. I mean, even back in elementary school, my teachers would write notes saying I had good ideas, but... I'd always forget to turn in my worksheets. Or I'd lose the instructions and just miss little details. My parents basically had to check my backpack every night just to make sure things got done. So... yeah.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things—like work, health, or everyday events—more days than not, even when there's no clear reason to worry?
Um... no, not really. I don't think so. I mean, I get frustrated when I mess up my work, but... I don't just sit around worrying about my health or random things. Just... normal stress, I guess.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or have trouble sitting still for long periods, like in meetings or while reading?
No, not really. I mean, I can sit still fine. I just... my mind wanders, but I'm not, like, bouncing off the walls or anything.

Besides your work or research tasks, do these attention and organization problems also cause noticeable issues in other areas of your life, like managing household responsibilities or your relationships?

Um... yeah, I guess it happens at home too. Like, I'll... I'll mean to do normal things. Just, you know, returning an email or paying a bill... or picking up groceries. And then... days go by, and I realize I never did it. It just... completely drops out of my mind.
Have you been feeling down, low in energy, or less interested in things you used to enjoy over the past few weeks or months?
Um... no. Not really. I don't think so. I don't feel down or anything... I still like doing my usual stuff. So, no.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks or keeping track of your belongings, like frequently losing keys, paperwork, or misplacing items you need?

Yeah, I guess. Um... my apartment and my laptop are kind of... they just look like a bunch of half-started projects. There's just stuff everywhere. Rent papers, gallery notes, article PDFs... to-do lists. I just... I have a hard time figuring out what actually needs to happen first. So it all just sort of piles up.
Do you use alcohol, recreational drugs, or have you noticed sleep problems—like trouble falling asleep or staying asleep—that might be contributing to your concentration difficulties?
Um... no. I don't really do drugs or anything. And... my sleep is fine. I usually sleep okay. So, no, I don't think it's that.
Have these attention and disorganization problems been going on consistently for at least the past six months, or did they start more recently?
Um... yeah, it's been a while. Since I moved to Boston, really. After I finished my bachelor's. So... maybe almost two years now? Yeah, about that long.
